title: Randomization commutes with noise
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $\rho\in\mathbb R$, let $f$ be a real-valued function on its outcome space, and fix an outcome $x$. As functions on the Boolean cube, randomizing the product noise transform of $f$ at $x$ equals applying the Boolean-cube noise operator with parameter $\rho$ to the function $r\mapsto R_rf(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses
$f$ is real-valued on the product outcome space
$x$ is an outcome in the product space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $x\in\Omega$. Then $r\mapsto R_r(T_\rho f)(x)$ equals $T_\rho(r\mapsto R_rf(x))$, with the noise on the right acting on the uniform Boolean sign cube.
